title: Light, not flow: why G-d's essence does not change while the world does
overview: Chapter 9 asks how G-d can say "I have not changed" when everything below Him changes: the world is renewed daily, judgement turns to kindness, and we pray for a new will. If the kindness and judgement of *Malchus* of *Asiya* come from the essence itself, the change seems to reach up to the essence. The answer is the *tzimtzum*. What comes down is a light, not a flow by cause and effect, so the source does not change. Even the light comes through *tzimtzumim*, like one projector behind different film slides: the projector stays the same, and only the images change. The change is in the receivers, us and all of creation. This holds for the encompassing and the inner light, and at every stage from the first *makom panui* down to *Malchus* of *Asiya*, a screen stands between each level and the next. Creation began in darkness, with a single *tzimtzum* of judgement straight to *Asiya*; every later stage begins with a *tzimtzum*, and new light comes through it. The will "before You" is the central will that transcends kindness and judgement, and in prayer we ask that it change judgement into kindness.

terms.gloss: contraction; plural *tzimtzumim*. What makes the change appear to the receivers; the source does not change
a flow of the thing itself, like water or money: the giver has less
light: it comes out and nothing is lost from its source
the line (and thread) of light drawn from the Essence of the infinite light; it begins with a *tzimtzum*
the empty place of the first *tzimtzum*, made to put the world in before the finite light is emanated into it
a screen or curtain between one level and the next, which the Malchus above breaks through
the light that fills all worlds in an individual way, as opposed to the encompassing light
the attribute of judgement; here, a single tzimtzum straight to Asiya
"may it be the will before You": the prayer in which we ask for a new will

sections.title: The question: everything comes from G-d's essence, so how can there be no change?
sections.summary: If the kindness and judgement of *Malchus* of *Asiya* come from the essence, and the world is renewed daily and we pray for a new will, then how can He say "I have not changed"?

phrases.he: (ט) אך הנה לכאורה אינו מובן
phrases.en: seemingly we have a question, something is not understood

phrases.he: מה שאמר אני יהו״ה לא שניתי
phrases.en: "I am G-d, I have not changed."

phrases.he: שזה מדבר במלכות דאין סוף עצמו
phrases.en: which, when it says "I", like we said before, "I" represents *Malchus*, and here we're talking about *Malchus* of *Ein Sof* itself.

blocks.text: This is the last of the nine introductory chapters, and it contrasts with the two before it. Those showed that everything is one unity: the stages of the *seder hishtalshelus* are all connected and work as one. This chapter explains that every stage comes through a *tzimtzum*. Although there is change and diversity from stage to stage, compared with the essence before the *tzimtzum* there is no real change. Understanding the *tzimtzum* at each stage is the other basic idea of the book.

The question starts from the verse "I, G-d, have not changed," quoted throughout the sources of *Kabbalah* and *Chassidus*. It is in Malachi, where G-d speaks to the Jewish people, and Rashi's simple explanation fits: G-d is patient and does not seem to punish the wicked, but His inner preference, that He wants good and righteousness, has not changed. Generally the verse is used to show that G-d is eternal, beyond change and unaffected by our world.

This verse speaks of the *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* itself. When it says "I", the "I" stands for *Malchus*, so this is G-d's essential self-expression, which does not change. But a question arises from what was explained in the last two chapters.

phrases.he: הרי אם בבחינת מלכות דעשיה יש בו שינוי בין דין לחסד, שהוא בחינת התפעלות כו',
phrases.en: if we witness that in *Malchus* of *Asiya* there is a change from, let's say, judgment to kindness and things like that, which is the idea of *hispaalus*, of having a reaction to what we're doing

phrases.he: מוכרח שגם במלכות דאין סוף יש שינוי זה
phrases.en: so then, seemingly, there must be this same corresponding change happening all the way back up to *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*, that at that highest level G-d seems to be responding and reacting to what we're doing

phrases.he: מאחר שאמר אני אני הוא כו' כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: because, like we said previously, it says, "I, I am he," that the *Malchus* of *Asiya* that we see is really the same as the *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* that is hidden within G-d's essence

blocks.text: If in *Malchus* of *Asiya* there is change from judgement to kindness, which is *hispaalus*, a reaction to what we do, then since everything is connected there must be the same change all the way up to the *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*. At that highest level G-d would seem to respond and react to us. Like the earlier "I, I am He", the *Malchus* of *Asiya* that we see is really the *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*, hidden within G-d's essence.

phrases.he: וכן מלכותך מלכות כל עולמים
phrases.en: and similarly, we quoted the verse, that G-d's kingship, his *Malchus*, is the *Malchus* of all the worlds

phrases.he: בשווא ממש כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: equally, like we said explained in the previous chapter

phrases.he: דהיינו כאשר עולה ברצונו הפשוט שבעצמות ממש, להיות חפץ חסד, הרי חפץ חסד העצמי הזה יורד עד למטה ממש בחפץ חסד דמלכות דעשיה
phrases.en: for example, when it arose in G-d's simple will within his essence to desire kindness, that desire for kindness is what's coming all the way down to *Malchus* of *Asiya* and being expressed as the physical kindness that G-d is giving us, life and health and *parnasa* and all these things

phrases.he: וכן להיפך כפי המובן מכל הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: and so to the opposite, G-d forbid, with judgment, based on what we've explained in the past few chapters

blocks.text: Likewise, "Your kingship is the kingship of all worlds" holds equally in every world. G-d's desire for kindness, which arises in His simple essential will, comes straight down to *Malchus* of *Asiya* and is expressed as physical kindness: life, health and a *parnasa*. The opposite holds too, G-d forbid, with judgement, as was explained in the last chapters.

phrases.he: וגם הרי
phrases.en: aside from this idea of being judged

phrases.he: בכל יום מחדש מעשה בראשית
phrases.en: just the very nature of the world itself is that every day G-d renews the works of creation

phrases.he: למטה מטה
שהוא בקדמין ובחוכמתא דבראשית ברא
phrases.en: so the world is being created with G-d's essential will and his essential wisdom

blocks.text: Aside from G-d reacting to what people do, the very nature of the world is that every day G-d renews the works of creation. The world is constantly changing, flowing from one state to another.

These changes come, as at the first creation, from G-d's essential will and wisdom. The word *reishis* in *Bereishis* means both *Keser* and *chachma*, so the world is created with G-d's essential will and essential wisdom. All the daily changes seem to come from these, all the way up to G-d's essence.

phrases.he: עד רום המעלות בעצמותו ממש
phrases.en: to all the way to G-d's essence

phrases.he: אם כן יש בחינת חידוש גם בעצמיות אור אין סוף
phrases.en: and if so, there seems to be something new, that G-d is like inventing some new ideas and coming up with new desires all the way in his essence, in the essence of the *Ein Sof*

phrases.he: ואיך אמר אני לא שניתי כלל
phrases.en: how can we say that? It says in the verse that G-d says, "I don't change, I haven't changed." How can we say there's no change?

phrases.he: וכן אנו אומרים אתה הוא קודם שנברא העולם כו'
phrases.en: similarly we say in the prayers, that G-d is the same just like he was before he created the world, he's exactly the same now after he created the world, that creating the world hasn't changed him

phrases.he: וכמו כן קודם שהאציל כו' וכידוע
phrases.en: just like there's no change from the process of creation, the same thing applies to before he emanated the world of *Atzilus*, that all of these stages of the *seder hishtalshelus* are not an essential change in G-d

blocks.text: So the changes seem to reach all the way to G-d's essence, a constant creative effort. If so, something new arises in the essence of the *Ein Sof*: G-d invents new ideas and new desires in His essence. How, then, can it say, "I have not changed at all"?

We say in the prayers that G-d is the same before the world was created and the same after. Creating the world did not change Him. Likewise before He emanated *Atzilus*: all the stages of the *seder hishtalshelus* are not an essential change in G-d.

phrases.he: ועל דרך משל מאדם התחתון, הרי יש שינוי גם ברצון העצמי מרצון של דין לרצון של חסד וכידוע
phrases.en: and if we're going to look at a metaphor, if we're comparing G-d, so to speak, to man, so we see that people, there can be this fundamental change in their desire from a desire for judgment to a desire for kindness, and they can really change their minds and change their feelings about things, which is a real *hispaalus*, a real reaction to things or a real change

phrases.he: ואיך אנו אומרים
phrases.en: and another question, how can we say that G-d is not reacting if we see that there's this idea of G-d judging the world and reacting to what we do

phrases.he: יהי רצון מלפניך, רצון חדש, שיתהפך רצון של דין לחסד כו'
phrases.en: we say *yehi ratzon milfanecha*, may it be the will before You. In other words, we're asking for a new will, for him to have a new will, to change his mind, to change a desire of judgment to one of kindness

blocks.title: A person whose desire changes
blocks.text: Compare a person. In him there is a change even in the essential will, from a desire for judgement to a desire for kindness. People really change their minds and feelings: a real *hispaalus*, a real reaction to things, or a real change.

Three more questions. First, if G-d judges the world and reacts to what we do, how is that not a change in Him? Second, creation itself, so diverse and changing every day, is a constant change. Third, when we pray *yehi ratzon milfanecha*, "may it be the will before You," we ask G-d to change His mind: a new will, turning judgement into kindness, tearing up the decree and giving us a good one.

phrases.he: ואנו רואין שנויים רבים בכל יום ושעה כו'
phrases.en: and we see that there's constantly changes every day, every moment

phrases.he: בכל אשר חפץ עשה תמיד בשמים ובארץ כו'.
phrases.en: like it says in *Tehillim*, that whatever G-d desires he does in heavens and the earth

blocks.text: We see constant change every day and every hour, and the verse in *Tehillim* says that whatever G-d desires He does in heaven and on earth. If everything comes from G-d's will, and the world is always changing, how is that not a change in G-d? If everything is united, with no intermediaries, and G-d directly chooses and creates all that happens, how can He not be changing?

The philosophers, like Aristotle, removed G-d from the picture because of this question: He is only an abstract force beyond everything, and creation happens through angels or lower forces that He creates. We say those are all a facade, and really it is Him. So how do we answer this question?

sensitivity.reason: Names the philosophers and Aristotle as a camp that removed G-d from creation: a loose characterisation of named thinkers under his name, and a sweeping one.
sensitivity.publishable: Some removed G-d from the picture because of this question: He is only an abstract force beyond everything, and creation happens through angels or lower forces that He creates. We say those are all a facade, and really it is Him. So how do we answer this question?
sensitivity.judgmentNote: The critique of an abstract, distant G-d is classical Chassidic position and can stay; whether the attribution to Aristotle and to philosophers as a camp must go is for a person to weigh against the class.

sections.title: The answer is tzimtzum: a light, not a flow, and only the receivers change
sections.summary: What comes down is a light, not a flow by cause and effect, and even the light passes through *tzimtzumim*, as a projector's light passes through film. The change is in the receivers alone, and the *tzimtzum* makes change appear without changing the source.

phrases.he: והתירוץ לכל זה הוא ענין הצמצום כידוע
phrases.en: and so the general answer to this is the idea of the *tzimtzum*

phrases.he: דאם היה השפע דרך עילה ועלול, היה נופל ענין שינוי התפעלות כו'
phrases.en: that if G-d were conducting the world in a process of cause and effect, where there was a direct connection or relationship between G-d and what He's creating, then it would be accurate to describe it with G-d changing and having this kind of reaction

blocks.text: The general answer is the *tzimtzum*, a recurring theme of this book at every stage. It is explained at length in chapters 12 and 13. What happens below reflects on G-d's essence, but He is not lowered by it: His essence remains beyond all of it. To see this, we look at each stage for its *tzimtzum*.
If the flow (*shefa*) came by way of cause and effect, with a direct link between G-d and what He creates, then it would be accurate to say that G-d changes and has a reaction.

phrases.he: אבל מאחר שההמשכה בבחינת אור וזיו לבד, וגם הוא על ידי צמצום, על כן אין בעצמות אלהו״ת שום שינוי כלל,
phrases.en: but since G-d is only creating the world with what's described as a light or a ray, and even that light and ray is not coming directly from Him, but only through a *tzimtzum*, so in the essence of G-d there is no real change

phrases.he: גם במלכות דמלכות דעשיה
phrases.en: even all the way down to the level of *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*, the essential G-dliness that's there that's driving that is staying the same, and it's just the way that it's expressed that's changing

blocks.text: But what is drawn down is only a light and a ray, and even that does not come directly from Him but through a *tzimtzum*. So in G-d's essence there is no change at all, all the way down to *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*. It always stays the same. What changes is only how it is revealed and how it appears to us; the essential G-dliness driving it stays the same.

phrases.he: וכך הוא עד רום המעלות
phrases.en: and that's true all the way up to the highest levels, that at each stage, all the appearance of changes and diversity that's happening with *seder hishtalshelus* is only happening because the *tzimtzum* gives that appearance, but the essence of what's going on there is not changing

phrases.he: ואחר הצמצום יש בחינת שינוי,
phrases.en: but after the *tzimtzum*, there are changes, and in other words, G-d does create this reality for us where we live in, where there are these changes, there is this diversity

phrases.he: וזהו מצד המקבלים לבד כידוע.
phrases.en: this level where things are changing is only from the perspective of the recipients, which is us and all of creation, but not from G-d's higher perspective

blocks.text: The same is true all the way up to the highest levels. At each stage the appearance of change and diversity is there only because the *tzimtzum* gives it, while the essence does not change. After the *tzimtzum* there are changes, and G-d does create the reality we live in, with its diversity. Alongside it there is a deeper level where nothing changes. The change is only from the side of the receivers, us and all of creation, and G-d sees and contains both.

The main point for now: we need to be aware of the *tzimtzum* and focus on it at every stage of the *seder hishtalshelus*. We look for how each stage connects up to G-d, and also for the *tzimtzum* and the fundamental level in it that does not change. That level changes only from our perspective.

phrases.he: וביאור ענין ההפרש בין אור לשפע ידוע לכל
phrases.en: and we talked about this in *Reb Hillel's* commentary, the difference between light and *shefa*

blocks.text: *Shefa* and *or* differ, which is well known and explained at length in *Chassidus*. Physically, when you give someone money or food, you no longer have it: that is a change from your side. Spiritually, when a teacher teaches a student, the teacher loses some of his mind space for the time. But *or*, light, is like watching someone and learning from them: each person appreciates it on his own level, and the one who shows it is not changed. It is like light through coloured glass. Reb Hillel's commentary has some of these metaphors, and more will come in chapters 12 and 13.

phrases.he: ואמנם גם בבחינת אור הוצרך להיות על ידי צמצום
phrases.en: but even the idea of light has to be that it's being revealed through a *tzimtzum* in order for us to have this relationship where the change is only apparent to us. So G-d is just revealing this essential light that's unchanging, but because it goes through a filter of a *tzimtzum* it takes on these different appearances to us

blocks.text: Even light has to come through a *tzimtzum*, so the change is only apparent to us. The essential light does not change; passing through the filter of the *tzimtzum*, it takes on different appearances to us.

blocks.title: The projector and the film slides
blocks.text: The basic metaphor is a projector. The projector is always the same, but because different slides of film are put in front of it, it projects different images. The deeper subtleties come later.

phrases.he: ועל כן צריך כל אדם לידע
phrases.en: and therefore every person needs to understand this idea of the *tzimtzum*

phrases.he: ענין הצמצום ולהתבונן בו בכל עולם לפי ערכו
phrases.en: and we have to study and analyze the *tzimtzum* in each stage in every level according to its nature, because the relationship with the *tzimtzum* is a little different in each stage

blocks.text: Every person must understand the *tzimtzum*. It is not enough to see the relationship as one of light. You must see how this light comes through a *tzimtzum*, and that is how you recognize that G-d does not change. Each stage has its own *tzimtzum* to study and analyze, because the relationship to it differs at each level.

phrases.he: כי הוא העיקר בכלל היחוד האלה״י באין שינוי לגבי העצמות
phrases.en: because understanding the *tzimtzum* and understanding the kind of the falseness of it, that it's, in a way, a deception to us, that's what allows us to see the main unity with G-dliness, and recognize that really G-d is not fundamentally changing at each stage

phrases.he: וכמו קמיה כחשיכה כאורה, רוחניות וגשמיות שוין, עד אצילות ועשיה שוין כידוע
phrases.en: like it says, "darkness and light are the same," that the spiritual and the physical are the same, and *Atzilus* and *Asiya* are the same, the highest world of G-dliness and the physical world that we live in are the same

blocks.text: This is the main point of the unity. Understanding the *tzimtzum*, and seeing that in a way it is a deception to us, is what lets us see the main unity with G-dliness: G-d is not fundamentally changing at each stage.
Darkness and light are the same, as it says; the spiritual and the physical are the same; and *Atzilus* and *Asiya*, the highest world of G-dliness and the physical world we live in, are the same.

sections.title: The encompassing light and the inner light do not change either
sections.summary: The equality of all things holds for the *makif*, which surrounds all worlds, and it holds for the inner light, which fills each stage. The verses "I have not changed" and "I fill the heavens and the earth" both speak of it.

phrases.he: הגם שזהו לגבי בחינת המקיף בלבד הנקרא סובב כל עלמין
phrases.en: even though this perspective that everything is equal is from the perspective of this surrounding light that's called the *makif*, which means the surrounding light, that is called *sovev kol almin*, the level that surrounds all the worlds, in other words in all the worlds

phrases.he: בכלל ובפרט
phrases.en: that's true both in the general, all-encompassing light and also at each stage there's that idea of the encompassing light at that stage

phrases.he: שלמעלה מהדרגת האור שבבחינת ממלא כל עלמין כידוע
phrases.en: and that essential light is something that's higher than the way the light is revealed in a step-by-step process which is called *memalei kol almin*, the way that G-d pervades and fills all the worlds in an individual way, as is known

blocks.text: The equality is only from the perspective of the encompassing light, the *makif*, called *sovev kol almin*, which encompasses all the worlds. That is true of the general encompassing light and of the encompassing light at each stage. The essential light is higher than the light revealed step by step as *memalei kol almin*, which fills all worlds in an individual way.

phrases.he: אך הנה גם בבחינת אור פנימי, בחינת ממלא בכלל ובפרט, אין שינוי כו'
phrases.en: but even in this second type of way that G-d is revealed, where He does reveal Himself within each stage differently, it's not a true change from His perspective

phrases.he: ועליון ותחתון שבו שוין
phrases.en: and even the highest and lowest levels within *memalei kol almin* are fundamentally the same from this deeper perspective

blocks.text: Even in the inner light, where He reveals Himself differently within each stage, there is no real change from His perspective. Even the highest and the lowest within *memalei kol almin* are fundamentally the same.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב אני לא שניתי, ואני הוא בחינת ממלא כידוע
phrases.en: like it says, "I have not changed," and again the word *ani* represents *Malchus*, which is the idea of *memalei kol almin*

phrases.he: וכן מה שכתוב את השמים ואת הארץ אני מלא,
phrases.en: and similarly the verse that says, "The heavens and the earth, I fill," again this *ani* is *memalei kol almin*, even though G-d is filling them, but He's filling them all

phrases.he: בהשוואה אחת דווקא מלא
phrases.en: equally

phrases.he: זה גם כן בבחינת אור פנימי וכמאמר לית אתר פנוי מיניה
phrases.en: and this idea of G-d how G-d fills everything refers also to *or pnimi*, like it says, there's no place that's empty from Him

phrases.he: כידוע

blocks.text: The verse says "I have not changed." The word *ani*, "I", stands for *Malchus*, the idea of *memalei kol almin*. The verse "I fill the heavens and the earth" is also about *memalei*: He fills them all equally, *davka*.

This is also the inner light, as it is said: there is no place empty of Him. Even within time and space, in the way G-d reveals Himself in the world, His essence is there, unchanged. We do not necessarily appreciate what we see, but it is really there, and uncovering that is the point of all this study.

phrases.he: והיינו משום דגם בבחינת ממלא בא ירידת האור והשפע על ידי צמצומים דוקא
phrases.en: and the reason that this is true is that even within *memalei kol almin*, even the way that G-d reveals Himself in an individual way where there are changes, but those changes are happening through *tzimtzumim* at every single stage

blocks.text: Why this is so: even in *memalei kol almin*, the descent of the light and the *shefa* comes only through *tzimtzumim*, at every stage. So the whole idea of *tzimtzum* is that it is only apparent, not a true change.

sections.title: A tzimtzum at every step, from the first line of light down to Malchus of Asiya
sections.summary: The line of light is drawn from the Essence through a first *tzimtzum*, and then through a screen between each level and the next, down to *Malchus* of *Asiya*, which is the King who alone is exalted.

phrases.he: וכידוע דגם בבחינת הקו וחוט שנמשך מעצמות אור אין סוף שנקרא ממלא כל עלמין דאבי''ע בכלל, הרי הוא נמשך על ידי צמצום בתחלה בעצמות
phrases.en: as is known, even the original finite line of light coming from the essence of the infinite light, which is this general idea of *memalei kol almin* of the four worlds of *ABYA*, begins first with a *tzimtzum*

phrases.he: והוא צמצום הראשון הנקרא מקום פנוי וחלל ריקן כו' כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים
phrases.en: that's described as the first *tzimtzum*, the empty place or the hollow, void, that G-d, so to speak, made an empty place to put the world, and then He emanated a finite light into it, like it's described in *Etz Chaim*

blocks.text: The line of light (*Kav*) drawn from the essence of the infinite light, which is *memalei kol almin* of the four worlds, begins first with a *tzimtzum* in the Essence. That first *tzimtzum* is called the *makom panui*, the empty and void place, as it is described in *Etz Chaim*. The same is true at every stage after it.

phrases.he: וכן בירידת הקו למטה בבחינת עגולים ויושר כו' עד שנעשה בחינת כתר לאדם קדמון הוא על ידי צמצום
phrases.en: so too the next stage, when the line of light then divides into two different modes, a mode that's described as circles and a mode that's described as straight emanations, until it becomes the crown of the original man, that's also through a *tzimtzum*

phrases.he: וכן מאדם קדמון לעתיק יומין ואריך אנפין כו'
phrases.en: and the same thing to go when the light goes from this *Adam Kadmon* stage, the original man, to the *Keser* of *Atzilus*, which is called the *Atik Yomin* and *Arich Anpin*, the ancient one and the patient one, that's also coming through a *tzimtzum*

blocks.text: As the line goes down, it divides into circles and straight lines, until it becomes the *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*, and that also comes through a *tzimtzum*. From *Adam Kadmon* to the *Keser* of *Atzilus*, called *Atik Yomin* and *Arich Anpin*, there is again a *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: וגם באצילות עצמו יש מסך בין כתר לחכמה בכלל
phrases.en: and so too within *Atzilus* there's a differentiation between all the *sefiros* that comes through a *tzimtzum*, so to go from the *Keser* of *Atzilus* to the *chachma*, there's a special type of *tzimtzum* that is described as a curtain

blocks.text: Within *Atzilus* too, between the *Keser* and the *chachma* there is a *masach*, a screen: a special kind of *tzimtzum*, described as a curtain.

phrases.he: והוא מה שכתוב והבדילה הפרוכת פרסא בין כו' כמו שכתוב בזוהר
phrases.en: like it says about the Temple, that there was a curtain that separated the holy of holies and the holy, and that's paralleling this separation between *Keser* and *chachma*, like it's described in the *Zohar*

phrases.he: וכן מאבא ואימא לזעיר אנפין ומזעיר אנפין לנוק' כידוע
phrases.en: and so too from the intellect of *chachma* and *bina* of *Atzilus* to the emotions of *Zeir Anpin* of *Atzilus*, there's again a *tzimtzum*, and so too from *Zeir Anpin* to *Nukva*, there's a special *tzimtzum*, as is known

blocks.text: The verse about the curtain that separated the holy of holies in the Temple parallels this separation between *Keser* and *chachma*, as the *Zohar* describes it. From the *chachma* and *bina* of *Atzilus* to the emotions of *Zeir Anpin* there is again a *tzimtzum*, and from *Zeir Anpin* to *Nukva* a special one. All this is in *Etz Chaim* and the *Zohar*, and here we learn it in *Chassidus*.

phrases.he: וממלכות דאצילות לבריאה יש מסך,
phrases.en: and again from the lowest level of *Atzilus* before the world of *Beriya* there's a *tzimtzum* described as a curtain

phrases.he: והמלכות בוקע המסך ונעשה כתר לבריאה
phrases.en: and *Malchus* pierces that curtain, and becomes the crown of *Beriya*

phrases.he: ועל דרך זה יש מסך בין בריאה ליצירה ומלכות דבריאה בוקע המסך ונעשה כתר ליצירה
phrases.en: and so too there's a curtain between *Beriya* and *Yetzira*, and it's this light of *Beriya* through piercing that curtain, that curtain is what makes it change and become the *Keser* of *Yetzira*

blocks.text: From the lowest level of *Atzilus* down to *Beriya* there is again a curtain. *Malchus* pierces it and becomes the *Keser* of *Beriya*. It is the same between *Beriya* and *Yetzira*: the light of *Beriya* pierces the curtain, and the curtain is what makes it change and become the *Keser* of *Yetzira*.

skip.note: The class does not read this line: after the words about the crown of Yetzira and "and so too", he goes on to line 45 without reading it.

phrases.he: עד מלכות דעשיה שנקרא המלך המרומם לבדו כו'
phrases.en: until the *Malchus* of our physical world, which is the G-dly force that's creating our physical world, which is described as the king who is exalted alone

blocks.text: *Malchus* of *Asiya*, the force that creates our physical world, is what is called the King who alone is exalted. Though He creates the physical world, His essence remains above it, transcendent above the world.

sections.title: Darkness first: the first thought was judgement, straight to Asiya
sections.summary: Creation began in darkness, and the first thought was a single *tzimtzum* of judgement straight to *Asiya*, which is the *tzimtzum* of the Name *Elokim* in *Malchus* of *Asiya*. Every stage begins with a *tzimtzum* of its own, and new light comes through it.

phrases.he: כמאמר רבותינו ז״ל כברייתו של עולם, ברישא חשוכא והדר נהורא
phrases.en: the world was created first with darkness, and then afterwards he returned light

blocks.title: The black goats
blocks.text: Our sages describe in the Talmud how someone asked why the black goats run ahead of the white ones. That is the nature of the world: it was created first with darkness, and afterwards light was returned.

So every stage begins with a *tzimtzum*, and then a new light is created through it. That is the idea of darkness first and then light, which is why we begin the day at night, with the day following the night.

phrases.he: וכן משאמרו רבותינו ז''ל בתחלה עלה במחשבה לברוא במידת הדין, שהוא בחינת הצמצום דשם אלהי״ם שבמלכות דעשיה
phrases.en: our sages say that originally G-d had in mind to create the world with the attribute of judgment, that's the idea that this *tzimtzum* comes first, the *tzimtzum* of the Name *Elokim* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*

blocks.text: Our sages say G-d first had in mind to create with the attribute of judgement, *midas hadin*: the *tzimtzum* of the Name *Elokim* in *Malchus* of *Asiya*. That *tzimtzum* comes first.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב בראשית ברא אלהי״ם, בחוכמתא, בקדמין, רצון וחכמה דמלכות דעשיה וכו' וד"ל:
phrases.en: like it says, in the beginning, *Elokim* created, in other words G-d created our world through *tzimtzum*, in His wisdom, in the beginning, that G-d's wisdom and will were filtered, so to speak, through the Name *Elokim*, and that's what allowed the creation of the world, which is the *ratzon* and *chachma* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*

blocks.text: The verse "In the beginning G-d created" means that He created our world through the *tzimtzum*: His wisdom and will were filtered, so to speak, through the Name *Elokim*, which made the creation of the world possible: the *ratzon* and *chachma* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*. At every stage we must look for the *tzimtzum*. From G-d's side it changes nothing; from ours it does.

sections.title: The will before You does not change; only what it becomes below does
sections.summary: The will "before You" transcends kindness and judgement, so prayer can change judgement into kindness in the world of action. The change is in the descent, not in the will itself.

phrases.he: ועפ"ז יתורץ הכל
phrases.en: based on this everything is answered

phrases.he: דמה שכתוב אני יהו״ה לא שניתי
phrases.en: whenever we speak about G-d not changing

phrases.he: בין רצון של חסד או דין בכל עולם דאבי''ע
phrases.en: and there's no difference to him between a desire of kindness or judgment, and that's true throughout the entire *seder hishtalshelus* in every world

phrases.he: היינו כמו שהוא קודם הצמצום ומסך שבוקע בו ונעשה כתר לעולם התחתון
phrases.en: that's from the perspective before the *tzimtzum* within that world; then within each world the light of that world goes through a *tzimtzum*, a curtain, and it becomes the desire for the lower world, and so those desires, there are changes on the other side of that curtain, but behind it there's not

blocks.text: This is the answer to "I, G-d, have not changed." Whenever we say G-d does not change, and that to Him there is no difference between a will of kindness and of judgement, that holds in every world of *ABYA*, from the standpoint before the *tzimtzum* of that world. Within each world the light passes through a *tzimtzum*, a curtain, and becomes the desire of the lower world. There are changes on the far side of that curtain, but not behind it.

By the way, I think the curtain metaphor comes partly from kings who sat behind a curtain so that people would not speak to them directly. Behind it they could be comfortable and send their messages out. There is a difference between the image of the king that is projected and the king himself, behind the curtain.

phrases.he: ועל זה אמר יהי רצון מלפניך דייקא
phrases.en: and this is why we, when we pray, say "may it be the will before You", in other words we're appealing to the central desire that's before the *tzimtzum* of each stage, all the way to G-d's essence, and we're asking that, since at that stage it transcends the differences of kindness and judgment, it can change it from judgment to kindness

blocks.text: So we pray *yehi ratzon milfanecha*: we appeal to the central desire before the *tzimtzum* of each stage, all the way to G-d's essence. That desire transcends the difference between kindness and judgement, so it can change judgement into kindness.

phrases.he: וכל בחינת מעלה ומטה שבעולם זה שוין כו'
phrases.en: and so too the whole idea of the hierarchies of our world to G-d are also the same, and so a person, for example, can have just as much of a connection to G-d, a simple person as a great *tzaddik*, even though on a certain level, when it comes to knowing Torah, there is a difference, and that's the idea of *memalei kol almin*, but in its essence it's not a real change

blocks.text: The same holds for the levels of our world: a simple person can have just as much connection to G-d as a great righteous man. On some levels, such as knowing Torah, there is a difference, which is the idea of *memalei kol almin*; in essence it is not a real change.

The simple takeaway: what G-d essentially wants is that we grow, change and learn. That is the same wherever you are, however high or low. There is always something to grow and learn, and that never goes away. You can know more, but serving G-d by growing is what does not change.

phrases.he: אבל אחר הצמצום נמשך הרצון בחכמה ומדות בשינויים עד מלכות דעשיה,
phrases.en: but after the *tzimtzum*, then G-d's desire does and his wisdom does come in a way of changes, and is in *middos*, until *Malchus* of *Asiya*, to actually G-d directing and changing our physical world

phrases.he: אומרים יהי רצון מלפניך, בשינוי לענין עשיה בפועל ממש, מדין לחסד וכהאי גוונא ודי למבין:
phrases.en: when we say *yehi ratzon milfanecha*, we ask G-d to make a practical, physical change in the world around us, changing it from judgment to kindness, and at that level there is a change

blocks.text: After the *tzimtzum*, G-d's will and wisdom come in changes, and in the *middos*, down to *Malchus* of *Asiya*, where G-d actually directs and changes our physical world. So when we say *yehi ratzon milfanecha*, we ask for a practical, physical change in the world, from judgement to kindness. At that level there is a change.

blocks.title: A parent who is strict and kind
blocks.text: Take a parent whose essential love for the child never changes. To educate the child, the parent sometimes puts on a face of strictness and sometimes of kindness: a mask, chosen for what best brings out the child's potential, always expressing the same love. When the child is ready to change and asks whether he can do it the good way instead of the hard way, the parent agrees. It depends on us. We will explain this at length in chapters 12 and 13, and in each chapter of the book.

reviewQuestions.question: Why does a change in what comes down not prove a change in G-d's essence?
What is the difference between *shefa* and *or*?
What does the projector stand for, and what changes in it?
Why does the inner light not change either?
What is the first tzimtzum, and from where is the line of light drawn?
What do we ask for when we say yehi ratzon milfanecha, and what is the will that does not change?
